Effective emotion regulation depends on developmental stage, measurement, and
context. My research examines regulation as a dynamic process unfolding across
behavior, physiology, and social relationships. Across these areas, a central
question guides my work: When, how, and under what conditions does regulation
support adaptation and well-being?

## Biopsychosocial Self-Regulation

Emotion regulation involves interconnected behavioral and physiological
processes. By examining these processes in real time, my research investigates
how regulatory patterns vary across development, measurement approaches, and
contexts. The same regulatory pattern can have different implications depending
on when, how, and in whom it is assessed.

{{< include _partials/research/fig-unfold.md >}}

## Stress, Adaptation, and Resilience

How adolescents cope with stress shapes their emotional and physical health. My
research examines how coping strategies, individual resilience, and family
resources influence adaptation. Effective coping depends on the fit between
coping responses, stressor demands, and available resources.

{{< include _partials/research/fig-stress.md >}}

## Family and Intergenerational Dynamics

Children develop regulatory capacities within interconnected family
relationships. My research examines how fathers, grandmothers, and broader
family dynamics shape regulation and adjustment. Physiological synchrony can
support or undermine regulation depending on the interaction context,
highlighting the importance of family relationships in children’s development.
